title: Volkswagen workers protest cutbacks at Emden wage talks
seoTitle: Emden VW workers protest wage talks

tea.why: Volkswagen management announced sweeping cost-cutting plans, job cuts, and the cancellation of ten collective bargaining agreements.
tea.want: Protesters and the union demanded a five percent pay increase and an end to proposed plant restructuring and benefit cuts.
tea.changed: Nov 24: The first round of wage negotiations in Emden ended without an agreement after lasting one and a half hours.

summary: Thousands of Volkswagen employees gathered in Emden, Lower Saxony, to protest against extensive austerity measures, wage freezes, and potential plant closures as the first round of collective bargaining talks began. Organised alongside union representation, workers marched with drums, red smoke, and symbolic black coffins outside the Nordseehalle venue. The negotiations between management and union representatives concluded after a brief session with no progress made, as both sides remained far apart on core issues. Union representatives warned that strikes could begin in January once the mandatory peace period expires, setting the next round of talks for December 15 in Zwickau.
demands: Rejection of proposed pay freezes for 2027 and 2028
Protection of the 35-hour workweek without schedule demands
Preservation of existing bonuses, allowances, and collective agreements
Job security and safeguarding of domestic plant locations
response: According to the sources, management representatives stated that the austerity measures and cost reductions are necessary due to severe cost pressures, dwindling cash, and weakened sales in the core brand, adding that they aim for a swift agreement before the end of the year.

updates.text: Thousands of Volkswagen employees gathered in Emden for a demonstration ahead of the wage negotiations.
The first round of negotiations concluded after one and a half hours without any agreement between the parties.
